title: French New Wave
description: French New Wave cinematography shoots fiction on locations with street light, handheld 16mm or 35mm, and an edit that will jump-cut rather than cover. The frame jumps into walking life: cafes, sidewalks, apartments with mixed practicals, and a camera that admits it is a camera.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Youth and impatience with studio polish. A character talks to the lens.
A walk is a burst of handheld, then a jump cut skips the boring meters. Paris oxygen, or any city's equivalent, is the lighting plot: windows, cafes, overcast streets.
It is not cinéma vérité. Vérité is documentary presence.

New Wave is authored fiction using documentary tools plus cinephile grammar (Jump Cut, freeze, iris, a look at the camera). It is also not found footage: there is no recovered tape, only a director in the street.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Location interiors, available or small practicals, 35mm or 50mm on a Cameflex-class body, handheld or a light tripod. Shoot the walk, then jump-cut in the edit.
Reflexive beats: eyeline to camera, a sudden insert. Street daylight, cafe tungsten, no matching backlight.
Prompt jump cuts implied, street light, jump-into-life framing, handheld Paris oxygen as location air, not as a mood word.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a young, restless fiction needs streets, jump cuts, and impatience with coverage. Do not use it for studio three-point polish or for a camcorder-horror premise.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Cinéma Vérité or Found Footage: a documentary claim, or a tape. The tell is a news timestamp, a horror shake, or glossy three-point.
Fix: keep it fiction, keep it location, handheld or light tripod, and let the edit jump.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is French New Wave in film?
A fiction look from late-1950s France and its heirs: location shooting, street and practical light, handheld cameras, jump cuts, and reflexive cinephile grammar. Studio polish is the enemy.
French New Wave vs Cinéma Vérité

Vérité documents real people and lets the filmmaker provoke. New Wave stages a story with the same cameras and streets, then jump-cuts and looks back at the lens. One is documentary method. The other is fiction with documentary tools.
When should I use French New Wave?
When a restless fiction belongs on a sidewalk or in a cheap apartment, and coverage would feel like a studio. Skip it for recovered-tape horror, for vérité documentary, or for billboard gloss.
How do I prompt French New Wave for AI image or video?

Write: French New Wave energy on [Subject], location street light, handheld 35mm, jump cuts implied, jump-into-life framing. Name the cafe or sidewalk. Do not add studio rims or a camcorder timestamp.
